facts.fact: Per studies from WPP (a third-party source cited by the page), ads following a clear problem-solution-benefit script convert up to 28% better.
facts.quote: According to studies from WPP, ads that follow a clear problem-solution-benefit script convert up to **28% better**.

facts.fact: The screen and script writing software market is projected to grow from USD 185.78 million in 2025 to USD 412.84 million by 2030 (a forecast the page attributes to no named source).
facts.quote: projected to grow from **USD 185.78 million in 2025 to USD 412.84 million by 2030**

facts.fact: The page's guidance is that a commercial's hook needs to land within the first 3 to 5 seconds of the ad.
facts.quote: It needs to land within the first **3 to 5 seconds** and can be a powerful visual

facts.fact: A 15-second TV commercial script has about 30-40 words to work with.
facts.quote: You've only got about **30-40 words** to work with, so there's absolutely no time for a winding story.

facts.fact: A 30-second TV commercial script has a comfortable word count of around 65-75 words.
facts.quote: With a comfortable word count of around **65-75 words**, you have enough runway to tell a complete mini-story

facts.fact: A 60-second TV commercial script runs about 150-170 words.
facts.quote: A 60-second script, which runs about **150-170 words**, lets you go deeper with storytelling

facts.fact: Per Adwave's own page, its AI can take a website URL and generate a complete, professionally formatted script (and matching video) in a few minutes.
facts.quote: Its AI can take your website URL and generate a complete, professionally formatted script (and the video to match) in just a few minutes.

facts.fact: Adwave states that its ad placement can get a commercial seen on major channels including NBC, ESPN, and Hulu.
facts.quote: getting your commercial seen on major channels like NBC, ESPN, and Hulu.

facts.fact: Adwave states it was designed specifically for small and medium businesses that do not have a marketing department.
facts.quote: It was designed specifically for small and medium businesses who don't have a marketing department but still need to get their message out there.

facts.fact: In the page's scripting terminology, VO stands for voiceover, meaning narration spoken by someone who isn't on screen.
facts.quote: **VO (Voiceover):** This is for any narration spoken by someone who isn't on screen.

facts.fact: In the page's scripting terminology, SFX stands for sound effects, meaning any sound that isn't music or dialogue.
facts.quote: **SFX (Sound Effects):** Any sound that isn't music or dialogue.

facts.fact: The article recommends a script length of 65 to 75 words for a 30-second commercial.
facts.quote: You're aiming for the sweet spot: **65 to 75 words** for a **30-second** spot.

facts.fact: The article states that a commercial's opening has about 3-5 seconds to hook the viewer.
facts.quote: You have about **3-5 seconds** to hook someone.

facts.fact: Adwave claims its AI can analyze a website and generate a complete broadcast-quality commercial, including script, visuals, and voiceover, in a few minutes (vendor's own claim, not independently verified).
facts.quote: can analyze your website and generate a complete, broadcast-quality commercial (script, visuals, and professional voiceover included) in just a few minutes.
